howToReach.summary: Most convenient – direct trains from Kolkata Howrah to Cox's Bazar (3.5–4 hours)

steps.detail: Trains: Tamralipta Express (12858), Kandari Express (18001), Duronto Express. Platform check at enquiry counter. Trains daily.
Cox's Bazar Flag Station is the terminus (~3.5 hrs). Auto-rickshaws outside for Old/New Cox's Bazar (₹30–50).
Tamralipta: 6:40 AM from Howrah. Kandari: 2:25 PM. Book at irctc.co.in or Howrah booking counter.

howToReach.summary: Frequent AC & non-AC buses from Esplanade Kolkata to Cox's Bazar (4–5 hours)

steps.detail: SBSTC, WBTC AC buses from Esplanade. Counter 1–4 for Cox's Bazar route. First bus 5:30 AM, last 8:30 PM.
Greenline AC (₹350), SBSTC Volvo (₹320), Non-AC (₹180). Buses every 30–60 minutes.

steps.point: Arrive at Cox's Bazar Bus Stand
steps.detail: Cox's Bazar Bus Stand is central. Take auto (₹30) or walk 15 min to Old Cox's Bazar Beach. Prepaid autos available.

howToReach.summary: Drive via NH16 – about 180 km, 4 hours from Kolkata

steps.detail: Take NH16 towards Kolaghat, then SH4 to Contai, then Cox's Bazar–Contai Road. Total ~180 km, 4 hours.
Tolls at Kolaghat (~₹100). Parking at Old Cox's Bazar Beach (₹50/day) and New Cox's Bazar (₹30/day).

travelTips.title: Best Time for Sunset
travelTips.answer: Old Cox's Bazar Beach offers the best sunset views. Reach by 5:00 PM in winter (4:45 PM in summer). The Marine Drive walkway is the prime viewing spot. Face west and look past the horizon for vivid orange skies.

travelTips.title: Swimming Safety
travelTips.answer: Swim only at Old Cox's Bazar Beach where the slope is gentle. Avoid New Cox's Bazar during high tide. Red flags mean no swimming. Lifeguards present at Old Cox's Bazar 6 AM–6 PM only. Always swim within marked zones.

travelTips.title: Cash & ATMs
travelTips.answer: Carry cash – many beachside stalls don't accept cards. SBI ATM at Old Cox's Bazar, HDFC ATM at New Cox's Bazar. UPI (PhonePe, GPay) works at most restaurants. Withdraw in Kolkata before travelling.

travelTips.title: What to Carry
travelTips.answer: Sunscreen SPF50+, hat, sunglasses, light cotton clothes, flip-flops, light jacket in winter, and a rain poncho in shoulder season. Keep valuables locked in hotel; don't carry to the beach.

mandarmani.name: Kuakata

famousPlaces.name: Red Crab Beach

famousPlaces.name: Kuakata Mohana

famousPlaces.name: Shankarpur Fishing Harbour

famousFoods.name: Fresh Crab Curry

famousFoods.name: Fried Pomfret (Rupchanda Bhaja)
famousFoods.description: Whole pomfret shallow-fried in mustard oil with lemon – beachside classic

famousFoods.name: Tiger Prawn Malai Curry

famousFoods.name: Bhapa Ilish (Steamed Hilsa)

howToReach.summary: Nearest station is Contai (Kanthi) – then 14 km by road to Kuakata

steps.detail: Trains: Tamralipta Express (12858), Kandari Express (18001). Get off at Contai (Kanthi) Station, ~3 hours from Howrah.
Auto-rickshaws and shared jeeps from Contai Station. 14 km, ~₹150–200 per auto, 30 minutes.
Tamralipta: 6:40 AM from Howrah. Kandari: 2:25 PM. Book at irctc.co.in. Alight at Contai, not Digha.

howToReach.summary: Direct buses from Kolkata Esplanade to Kuakata via Contai (5 hours)

steps.detail: SBSTC buses to Contai, then local bus to Kuakata. Counter 5–6 for Contai route. Some direct buses available.
SBSTC AC (₹320 to Contai), then local bus (₹30). Total ~5 hours. First bus 6 AM.
Kuakata More on Contai-Digha Road. Take auto (₹50) to beach, 4 km. Shared autos available.

howToReach.summary: Drive via NH16 to Contai, then 14 km to Kuakata (4.5 hours from Kolkata)

steps.detail: NH16 to Kolaghat, SH4 to Contai, then Contai–Kuakata Road. Total ~170 km, 4.5 hours.
Beach parking at resorts (₹50–100/day). Drive on hard sand at low tide only – check tide timings.

travelTips.title: Beach Buggy Rides
travelTips.answer: Beach buggies and ATV rides near the main beach entry. ₹300–500 per ride. Best at sunrise/sunset when the sand is firm. Avoid during high tide when the beach narrows significantly.

travelTips.title: Red Crab Spotting
travelTips.answer: Walk the beach at sunrise (5:30–6:30 AM) to see thousands of red crabs. Don't chase them – they burrow into wet sand. Best near the Mohana river mouth. Bring binoculars and a camera with zoom.

travelTips.title: Tide Timing
travelTips.answer: Check tide timings before driving on beach. High tide submerges parts of the 13 km stretch. Local resorts post daily tide charts. Best beach driving: 2 hours after high tide. Avoid evenings in rainy season.

travelTips.title: Cash & Connectivity
travelTips.answer: Limited ATMs in Kuakata – carry cash from Kolkata or Contai. BSNL and Jio work well; Airtel patchy. Most resorts accept UPI. Stock up at Contai before entering Kuakata village.

famousPlaces.name: Sajnekhali Watch Tower
famousPlaces.description: Prime wildlife viewing tower with mangrove interpretation center

famousPlaces.name: Dobanki Watch Tower

famousPlaces.name: Netidhopani Watch Tower
famousPlaces.description: Scenic tower with views of tiger habitat and ancient ruins

famousFoods.description: Freshly caught mud crab from the mangroves in spicy local gravy

famousFoods.description: Hilsa from the tidal rivers, steamed with mustard paste – Bengal classic

howToReach.summary: Train to Canning from Sealdah, then boat to Satkhiras (most common route)

steps.detail: Local trains to Canning: 1.5 hours. Trains every 30 min from Sealdah. First train 4:30 AM. Canning is the railhead for Satkhiras.
From Canning Station, auto/toto to Godkhali (45 min, ₹50). Godkhali is the main boat jetty for Satkhiras.
Permitted boats Godkhali–Sajnekhali (3–4 hrs). Shared boats ₹500–1000, private ₹3000+. Book via tour operator or forest dept.

howToReach.summary: Bus to Sonakhali or Namkhana, then boat into the mangroves

steps.detail: SBSTC buses to Sonakhali (3 hrs, ₹80) or Namkhana (4 hrs, ₹100). First bus 6 AM from Esplanade, Kolkata.
From Sonakhali jetty, boats to Sajnekhali (2.5 hrs). From Namkhana, boats to Bhagabatpur. Book at jetty or via tour operator.

howToReach.summary: Drive to Godkhali (110 km from Kolkata), then boat into the forest

steps.detail: Take Basanti Highway via Baruipur to Godkhali. ~110 km, 3 hours. Park at Godkhali jetty (₹50/day).
Book at Godkhali Tourist Counter or pre-book with Help Tourism, Satkhira Tiger Camp. Day trips ₹1500–3000 per person.

travelTips.title: Forest Permit is Mandatory
travelTips.answer: Get permits from the Forest Department at Sajnekhali or via tour operators. Foreigners need passport copy + visa. Apply 2 weeks ahead in peak season. Cost: ₹40 (Indians), ₹150 (foreigners). No permit = no entry.

travelTips.title: Hire a Local Guide
travelTips.answer: Mandatory for all safaris. Guides know tiger movement patterns, bird calls, and safe trails. Cost is included in most tour packages. Never enter the forest without a certified guide – it is also illegal.

travelTips.title: Best Wildlife Viewing
travelTips.answer: Early morning (6–9 AM) and late afternoon (3–5 PM) boat safaris offer best sightings. Visit watch towers at Sajnekhali, Dobanki, Netidhopani. Stay silent – noise scares wildlife. Bring binoculars.

travelTips.title: Carry Mosquito Protection
travelTips.answer: Mangroves have heavy mosquito and insect activity. Carry DEET repellent, full-sleeve clothing, and anti-malarial medication. Avoid scented products. Best to visit in dry winter months (Nov–Feb).
